extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation across five dimensions: instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis. It covers 25 tasks with 6092 QA pairs.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
extraction.citeAs: Luo, Yulin et al. RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv:2510.17801v1, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: To evaluate five cognitive dimensions, the benchmark builds datasets from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Instruction comprehension uses paired explicit and implicit instructions, where explicit instructions are drawn from daily-life scenarios and implicit instructions are rewritten from them using LLMs. Perception reasoning uses real robot data with type and view metadata, curated static attributes, GPT-generated functional properties and distractors, Gemini-segmented video steps, manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes, and human-labeled bounding boxes. Generalized planning is built from high-quality robotic videos by extracting frame sequences as standardized inputs. Affordance prediction samples representative frames from the planning pool and annotates them with static, dynamic, and mobile affordances. Failure analysis uses execution-level failures collected from RoboMIND and planning-level failures synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions due to lack of real-world planning failure data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The data combine large-scale real-world robotic datasets and curated in-house collection. For planning, the benchmark uses high-quality robotic videos from sources including Open X-Embodiment, RH20T, RoboMIND, and other cited robotic datasets, extracting frame sequences as standardized inputs. Perception uses real robot data, curated object attributes, segmented videos, and human-labeled bounding boxes.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions, including wrong object, missing step, and wrong order. Explicit instructions are rewritten into implicit demand-based requests using LLMs. For planning, each step is mapped into function templates grouped into manipulation or navigation skill lists. Data are standardized into multiple-choice QA for perception tasks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The benchmark customizes data workflows for each dimension and generally follows preprocessing, annotation, and Q&A generation stages. For planning, frame sequences are extracted as standardized inputs from videos. General and task-specific filters are applied during construction, addressing image quality and task validity, such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks. After construction, items that all models solve correctly are removed, and items that all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are provided by MLLMs and humans depending on the task. For perception reasoning, GPT generates functional properties and distractors, Gemini segments video steps for temporal grounding, manual annotations provide relative positions and keypoint changes, and humans label bounding boxes linking instructions to target objects. For planning, Gemini generates structured annotations including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata such as objects, actions, scenes, and embodiments, which are then refined by human annotators. Affordance prediction uses annotations of static contact points, dynamic motion trajectories, and mobile base positions. Failure analysis uses expert labels for execution-level failures. A post-construction quality inspection is conducted by 20 professionally trained annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A two-stage quality control process is used: data filtering during construction and post-construction validation. After construction, 20 professionally trained annotators validate linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is adopted: items that all models solve correctly are removed, while items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators; expert annotators with prior training were also used in the human study on planning data.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LLMs, GPT, Gemini, MLLM, VLMs, detection models
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench is intended to provide a unified scaffold to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that current planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements, which may contribute to poor cross-embodiment planning. It also notes that tasks involving uncommon objects, symbolic reasoning, or world knowledge lead to performance drops, while common, well-seen objects remain relatively acceptable.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark reports several limitations in current models and some data limitations. Models show severe degradation on implicit instructions, weak robot-view recognition and temporal grounding, shallow affordance prediction, and poor execution-level failure diagnosis. For data, real-world planning failure data are lacking, so planning-level failures are synthesized. Human performance on execution-level failure diagnosis is also relatively low, underscoring intrinsic task difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains in robotic manipulation. It is used for systematic evaluation across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis, and for establishing leaderboards and comparing model performance, including human and text-only baselines.
